detail.longDescription: When rendering a Quarto document with jupyter: python3 , calling sklearn 's learning_curve() with n_jobs=-1 crashes with a TerminatedWorkerError . The same code runs fine in a plain Jupyter notebook. Here's a minimal reprex; save this as test.qmd and run quarto render test.qmd : --- title: "reprex" format: pdf jupyter: python3 --- ```{python} #| error: true from sklearn.datasets import make_classification from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier from sklearn.model_selection import learning_curve X, y = make_classification(n_samples=1000, random_state=42) train_sizes, train_scores, test_scores = learning_curve( KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=5), X, y, cv=5, n_jobs=-1 ) ``` This give me TerminatedWorkerError: A worker process managed by the executor was unexpectedly terminated. This could be caused by a segmentation fault while calling the function or by an excessive memory usage causing the Operating System to kill the worker. Changing n_jobs=-1 to n_jobs=1 resolves the error, but loses parallelism. Is there a clean way to use multiple cores inside a Quarto document? Here's my session info: OS: Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0 Quarto: 1.10.18 Python: 3.13.5 scikit-learn: 1.9.1 joblib: 1.6.0 jupyter_client: 8.10.0 jupyterlab: 4.6.3 Detailed traceback: TerminatedWorkerError: A worker process managed by the executor was unexpectedly terminated. This could be caused by a segmentation fault while calling the function or by an excessive memory usage causing the Operating System to kill the worker.
